title: bug: JetBrains drops latestCheckRun.outcome, so a non-passed exit-0 check displays as passed
description:
Unowned residual found while re-planning CQ-I06 (architect-8419009e, chan-18116c9a msg-b280b4ba, 2026-10-31 16:36Z). This is V12's client hand-forward.

The daemon side is DONE. CQ-V12b (task-6339299a) projects `latestCheckRun.outcome` in deliveryProjection.

The JetBrains client never reads that field. It reads only `command`, `exitCode` and `source`:
- `moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt`: DeliveryCheckRun has no outcome;
- `moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJson.kt` (around :440): parses only those three fields;
- `moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/DeliveryPresentation.kt` (around :22-29): renders from exitCode alone.

So a check that exited 0 but whose recorded outcome is timeout, infra-failure, skipped, inconclusive or code-failure renders in task detail exactly like a pass. That is misleading delivery evidence.

Scope: JetBrains only (it is the primary IDE). VS Code renders no latestCheckRun at all; whether it should gain a delivery-check view is a parity decision for the human, out of scope here.

History: task-fee5e136 (2026-09, LOW, archived with its old epic on 10-24) covered the earlier, pre-`source` version of this display bug. This row is the outcome half, which landed later.

Off-lane: no open row declares any of the files below, so this row needs no wrapper-lane slot.

Expected files:
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJson.kt
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/DeliveryPresentation.kt
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties
- moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/DeliveryPresentationTest.kt (plus a MoeJson parse test if one exists)

Owner record: CQ-I06 (task-4e412148) step 1 names this row as the owner of the hand-forward residual.
definitionOfDone: DeliveryCheckRun in Models.kt carries the projected `outcome`. MoeJson parses `latestCheckRun.outcome` when present and leaves it null when absent, so an older daemon without the field still parses.

DeliveryPresentation renders a recorded non-passed outcome (timeout, infra-failure, skipped, inconclusive, code-failure) as NOT passed, even when exitCode is 0. A 'passed' outcome renders as passed. With no outcome it keeps today's exit-code rendering. User-visible strings live in MoeBundle.properties.

JUnit tests cover at least: exitCode 0 with outcome 'timeout' renders not-passed; exitCode 0 with outcome 'passed' renders passed; no outcome falls back to the existing rendering; MoeJson parses the field and tolerates its absence.

A fresh `cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test` exits 0. On this host run the Windows equivalent under the jetbrains-gradle lease, labelled as such, and supply the output to complete_task. Never build in place in the shared checkout (GLOBAL rule 0).
No VS Code change. The completion summary states that VS Code has no latestCheckRun view and that parity is a human decision.

implementationPlan.description:
Model, parser and parser tests (DoD 1, plus the parse half of DoD 3). Write test (c) first and watch it fail, then implement.

1. Models.kt:164. Append `val outcome: String? = null` as the LAST parameter of DeliveryCheckRun, so the positional 3-argument calls (MoeJson.kt:441, DeliveryPresentationTest) still compile. Give it a one-line KDoc: the REPORTED daemon CheckOutcome (passed, code-failure, infra-failure, timeout, skipped or inconclusive; packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts:1544), verbatim. It is null when the daemon predates CQ-V12b or the run was recorded without an outcome.

2. MoeJson.kt:441-444 (parseDelivery). Pass `outcome = it.getStrictStringOrNull("outcome")`.
- Keep the JSON string verbatim: no trim, no case-folding, NO whitelist.
- Absent, JSON null or a non-string (number, boolean, array including ["timeout"], object) gives null. So an older daemon without the field still parses.
- Why no whitelist, unlike `source`: step 2 fails closed on every outcome except exactly "passed". A whitelist would turn an unknown future outcome into null, fall back to the exit-code verdict and reopen this bug.

3. MoeJsonTest.kt.
(a) The deliveryJson at line 23: add "outcome":"code-failure" to latestCheckRun (its exitCode -9 matches). This is required: serializeNulls would otherwise emit "outcome":null on the round trip, and that test would fail.
(b) The wrong-kinds test at lines 56-62: input "outcome":["timeout"], expected "outcome":null.
(c) A NEW test through bothPaths(blockerTaskJson(...)), which covers both the snapshot and single-task paths:
- absent gives null;
- each of the six CheckOutcome values comes back verbatim;
- "cancelled" gives "cancelled", " timeout " gives " timeout ", and "" gives "";
- 42, true, null, ["timeout"] and {} give null.
Read the value via serializedDelivery(task).asJsonObject.getAsJsonObject("latestCheckRun").get("outcome"). That way the test compiles on the old model and is RED there (mem:pattern-jetbrains-red-for-new-model-fields). Add the older-daemon case: {"command":"node gate.cjs","exitCode":0,"source":"runner-observed"} keeps all three values, with outcome null.

Edit tracked files only with the Edit tool (GLOBAL rail). Error handling: parsing stays total. A malformed outcome never throws and never drops command, exitCode or source.
implementationPlan.note: DeliveryCheckRun gains trailing `outcome: String? = null` (KDoc). parseDelivery reads it via getStrictStringOrNull, verbatim, no whitelist. MoeJsonTest: fixture (a) +outcome code-failure, wrong-kinds (b) outcome ["timeout"] -> null, two new tests (verbatim/wrong-kind matrix over bothPaths; older-daemon payload keeps command/exitCode/source). GREEN: MoeJsonTest 32/0/0, DeliveryPresentationTest 9/0/0. Peer dirty paths (.moe/*, scripts/moe-agent.*, scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs) untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
Presentation, bundle and presentation tests (DoD 2, plus the render half of DoD 3). Write the tests first.

1. DeliveryPresentation.kt:24-28. Replace the verdict that reads exitCode alone. Use a local `val run = delivery.latestCheckRun`. Mirror the daemon's gate rule from recordCheckRun.ts:51: only an outcome of passed, or a legacy report with no outcome at exit 0, can ever satisfy a gate.
- `passed = code == 0 && (run.outcome.isNullOrEmpty() || run.outcome == "passed")`. The comparison is exact and case-sensitive.
- passed gives moe.delivery.checkPassed (PASS).
- code != 0 gives moe.delivery.checkFailed (FAIL), today's label. That includes a contradictory 'passed' at a nonzero exit, which the daemon refuses to record anyway.
- Anything else gives the NEW key moe.delivery.checkNotPassed (FAIL): exit 0, but the recorded outcome is not passed.
Right after the verdict row and before checkSource, call `addValue("moe.delivery.checkOutcome", run?.outcome)`.
- The value is the raw reported token, verbatim. It is data, not UI text, like source and attemptPhase.
- addValue already skips null and "", so "" counts as absent.
- An outcome with no exitCode yields only the outcome row.
Keep the 'REPORTED, never proof' comment. TaskDetailDialog needs no change: it renders labelKey plus value literally via JBTextArea.

2. MoeBundle.properties, delivery block at lines 257-268. Use ASCII only and the Edit tool, and preserve every other byte. Add:
- `moe.delivery.checkNotPassed=Reported check did not pass - exit code`, after checkFailed;
- `moe.delivery.checkOutcome=Reported check outcome`, before checkSource.

3. DeliveryPresentationTest.kt. Add tests that assert exact row lists (labelKey, value and outcome):
(1) exit 0 with each of timeout, infra-failure, skipped, inconclusive, code-failure, cancelled, Passed and " passed", with a command and a source, gives [checkCommand, (checkNotPassed,"0",FAIL), (checkOutcome, outcome), checkSource]. Also assert that no row has labelKey checkPassed or outcome PASS.
(2) exit 0 with "passed" gives [checkCommand, (checkPassed,"0",PASS), (checkOutcome,"passed"), checkSource].
(3) exit 1 and exit -9, each with null, "passed", "timeout" and "code-failure", give the checkFailed row with FAIL, plus the outcome row when the outcome is non-null.
(4) No outcome: null and "" at exit 0 each give exactly [(checkPassed,"0",PASS)], today's rendering.
(5) DeliveryCheckRun(outcome = "timeout") with no exitCode gives [(checkOutcome,"timeout")].
(6) In 'every emitted bundle key has a translation', add rows(TaskDelivery(latestCheckRun = DeliveryCheckRun(exitCode = 0, outcome = "timeout"))) and change 12 to 14.
Existing tests stay unchanged and green, because their fixtures carry no outcome. Change no VS Code, daemon or docs file.
implementationPlan.note: DeliveryPresentation: passed = code==0 && (outcome null/empty || exactly "passed"); key = checkPassed (PASS) / checkFailed (code!=0, FAIL) / checkNotPassed (exit 0 non-passed, FAIL); then addValue(checkOutcome, raw outcome) before checkSource. Outcome hoisted into a local (no lambda smart-cast reliance). Bundle: +checkNotPassed after checkFailed, +checkOutcome before checkSource (ASCII, Edit only). Tests: 5 new (non-passed matrix incl. cancelled/Passed/" passed" with no-PASS assertion; passed; nonzero x {null,passed,timeout,code-failure}; null/"" fallback; outcome-only) + bundle-key count 12->14. RED: 14 tests, 5 failed (AssertionError), 0 errors. GREEN: DeliveryPresentationTest 14/0/0, MoeJsonTest 32/0/0 (snapshot /mnt/d/moe-scratch/344a-iter-Rm4PkX, jetbrains-gradle lease, released).

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
JetBrains task detail shows a reported check as passed only when exitCode is 0 AND the daemon-projected latestCheckRun.outcome is absent, empty or exactly 'passed'. DeliveryCheckRun carries latestCheckRun.outcome verbatim, or null when it is absent or not a JSON string, so an older daemon still parses.

A non-passed or unknown outcome at exit 0 renders the FAIL row 'Reported check did not pass - exit code', followed by a 'Reported check outcome' row with the raw token. 'passed' at exit 0 renders as passed, plus the outcome row. A nonzero exit always renders 'Reported check failed - exit code'. With no outcome, today's exit-code rendering is unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: exitCode 0 with outcome timeout, infra-failure, skipped, inconclusive or code-failure (or an unknown or case-variant token) renders moe.delivery.checkNotPassed (FAIL) plus moe.delivery.checkOutcome, and never moe.delivery.checkPassed or PASS.
exitCode 0 with outcome 'passed' renders moe.delivery.checkPassed (PASS) plus the outcome row.
A null or empty outcome renders exactly today's rows. A nonzero exit renders moe.delivery.checkFailed (FAIL) whatever the outcome.
MoeJson parses latestCheckRun.outcome verbatim when it is a JSON string, and as null otherwise. A payload without the field parses with command, exitCode and source intact.
The labelled Windows-equivalent full JetBrains test suite exits 0 in a fresh HEAD snapshot under the jetbrains-gradle lease.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Whitelist outcome the way `source` is whitelisted: REJECTED. A whitelist turns an unknown future outcome into null, the verdict then falls back to exit code, and an exit-0 non-pass reads as passed again. The fail-closed render covers unknown values instead.
2. One bundle key per outcome value: REJECTED. source and attemptPhase are already shown as raw tokens, so two keys are enough.
3. Reuse checkFailed for exit 0 with a non-passed outcome: REJECTED. 'failed - exit code 0' reads skipped or inconclusive as a code failure. The new checkNotPassed label is accurate.
4. Every non-passed outcome renders checkNotPassed even at a nonzero exit: REJECTED. That changes today's 'failed' label for nonzero exits. The minimal delta touches the exit-0 rows only.
5. Split parse and render into two tasks: REJECTED. They are one contract over six small files, and the DoD names all of them. The 6-file count floors the tier to heavy; that is accepted.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- The daemon's projection (deliveryProjection.ts) omits an outcome that is not a CheckOutcome. recordCheckRun refuses passed at a nonzero exit and code-failure at exit 0, so the client's 'nonzero + passed' branch is purely defensive.
- In TaskDetailDialog, DeliveryRow.outcome is semantic only. What the user sees is the bundle label plus the literal value, so the label must not say 'passed' for a non-passed run.
- MoeJsonTest serializes with serializeNulls. Adding a model field therefore breaks the two existing delivery round-trip assertions until their JSON names the field.
- Files are LF and UTF-8.
- No doc describes the JetBrains delivery rows: a grep of docs/ for 'Reported check' or latestCheckRun found none, so there is no docs change.
